pet.name: Worldstorm Dragon
pet.scope: Independent second visual pass of the exact private v2 candidate only; not canonical or live approval.

independentFindings: I inspected the exact-hash raw source and battle sheets for all 13 clips at six phases, including front, side, head-front, head-side, and opposite-side head views. The head silhouette stays continuous through idle, movement, attacks, death, revive, and attack-sequence poses. The prior visibly flattened head is not present in these v2 images.

I inspected the corrected low and medium production-runtime sheets for both source and battle stages: 16 transitions, six phases, front and side, head and body. Head-to-neck connection remains coherent, with no visible neck stretch or skull flattening. Death and revive retain the authored motion; at the most rotated samples the close head view is partly cropped by camera framing, while the full-body sheet shows the connected pose.

I inspected all 24 companion idle frames and all nine equipped techniques in front and side, 12 phases per view. No face or neck distortion is visible in the idle or technique poses. The technique captures show model pose and shape; they do not evaluate combat effects.
I inspected the atlas material evidence; no visible surface break or missing region was found.
No asset, canonical roster, or tracker file was modified by this review.

companionPreview.renderer: Production PetYardModelStage component bundle with exact private battle bytes injected

atlas.applicability: current atlas image inspected; no visible holes or missing surface regions

packageNote: The initial release package contained runtime sheets from an older Worldstorm candidate. I rejected those sheets because their model hashes did not match this candidate. This review uses the corrected runtime/low and runtime/medium files whose manifests pin the source and battle hashes above; their eight rendered sheet hashes were independently checked against disk.
limitations: This PASS applies only to the exact private candidate hashes listed above. It does not establish canonical promotion or deployment to live.
Extreme body tumble causes partial crop in close head framing; the full-body views retain the connected model and pose.
